ap_biology-f01.title: A test cross in fruit flies

stimulus.description: A student sets up several vials, and in each vial crosses a fruit fly that is heterozygous for a dominant allele for long wings with a fly that is homozygous recessive and has vestigial (short) wings. All of the vials are kept at the same temperature and given the same food. The gene is on an autosome. After the offspring emerge, the student counts a total of 400 offspring and records the number with long wings and the number with vestigial wings.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe how the two alleles of a gene separate during meiosis in a heterozygous fly.
parts.model_answer: The homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I, so each gamete receives only one of the two alleles of the gene.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives a correct description of the biological concept or process
required_elements: The homologous chromosomes separate during meiosis, so each gamete receives one allele of the gene
alt_solutions: each gamete gets only one of the two alleles because the homologs are separated
segregation puts the two alleles into different gametes
common_errors: says each gamete receives both alleles
says the alleles are combined into one allele in the gamete
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify one factor that should be kept the same in all of the vials, and explain why it should be kept the same.
parts.model_answer: The temperature at which the larvae develop (or the food or the age of the parents) should be the same in all vials, so differences in the offspring are not caused by the environment.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies an appropriate feature of the experimental design and gives the reason
required_elements: Names a factor held constant and links it to reducing environmental effects on the phenotype
alt_solutions: the temperature of development should be the same so the phenotype is not changed by the environment
the food supplied should be the same so that wing size is not affected by nutrition
common_errors: names the genotype of the parents as the factor to keep the same, with no reason
names a factor without connecting it to the comparison of offspring
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: State a null hypothesis for a chi-square test of the offspring counts.
parts.model_answer: The observed numbers of long-winged and vestigial-winged offspring do not differ from the 1:1 ratio expected from the test cross, other than by chance.

rubric_rows.criterion: States an appropriate null hypothesis
required_elements: States that there is no difference between the observed offspring counts and the expected 1:1 ratio
alt_solutions: any difference from a 1:1 ratio is due to chance alone
the data fit the expected 1:1 ratio of long to vestigial offspring
common_errors: states a prediction that the ratio will be 3:1
states that the observed counts will be very different from the expected counts
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The student calculates a chi-square value of 2.25 for the observed counts of 215 long-winged and 185 vestigial-winged offspring. Using the critical value of 3.84 (df = 1, p = 0.05), state whether the null hypothesis can be rejected, and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The chi-square value of 2.25 is less than the critical value of 3.84, so the null hypothesis cannot be rejected; the difference from the 1:1 ratio can be explained by chance.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the prediction or result with biological reasoning
required_elements: The value 2.25 is less than 3.84, so the null hypothesis is not rejected and the difference from 1:1 is due to chance
alt_solutions: the calculated value is below the critical value, so the data are consistent with the expected ratio
fails to reject the null hypothesis because 2.25 does not exceed 3.84
common_errors: concludes that the null hypothesis is rejected even though 2.25 is below 3.84
compares the value with the wrong critical value and gives no reason
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.prompt: Explain how an error in meiosis such as nondisjunction can produce an egg with an abnormal number of chromosomes.
parts.model_answer: In nondisjunction a pair of homologous chromosomes or a pair of sister chromatids fails to separate, so one gamete receives an extra chromosome and another gamete is missing one.
